objections.title: The gain needs no forecast: with no gap forecast and no end signal the engine is at 0.71 s, against 0.66 s for rules 1+3 and 0.51 s for exact hints
objections.claim_hit: PAPER_PLAN 'The claim' and contribution rows 1, 4 and 5 (forecasts from the agent drive eviction, staging and pins; exact hints add 0.96 s; just-in-time timing 18 %); PAPER_INTRO paragraph 4 and contributions 2-3 ('exact return times cut mean TTFT a further 2.9x [1.47 -> 0.50 s]'); DECISIONS 'rules 1 and 3 reach the exact-hint arm's level'.
objections.why_serious: On the 6,715 returning turns all eleven runs share: original HiCache 5.47 and 6.62 s, nofc_noend (reads at arrival, LRU with queued turns last) 0.71 s, nofc 0.69, ec_r1 0.67, ec_r13 0.66, JIT exact 0.51. So 96 % of the way to exact hints uses no forecast and no end signal, and against that rival exact hints are worth 1.4x (0.71 -> 0.51), not 2.9x. Three-quantile hints add 0.056 s there (within-pair 5-95 %: -0.02 to +0.15) and 0.143 s on the 11,198 turns of the five leading arms; of that net, 66 % sits in the second load episode alone (1,519 turns), 23 % in the first, 10 % in the last 14 minutes, and 1 % (+0.003 s per turn) on the other 7,008 turns. Reruns of one arm moved 0.25-0.28 s. What carries the gain (read pins, queued-turn protection, gate and hold, re-reads) is what PAPER_INTRO itself lists as prior art (CachedAttention, Bidaw).
objections.how_to_answer: Make the queue-aware hint-free engine the baseline of record and state the hint's increment over it in seconds beside the rerun spread: 44 users, 70 GB: +0.05 to +0.15 s TTFT for three quantiles, +0.20 s for exact hints, 22 % and 31 % fewer SSD pages. Replace '2.9x' by '1.4x over a queue-aware hint-free engine, exact hints only'; replace the 'share of the gain' column (96-98 % hides 0.51 / 0.66 / 0.71 s, a 29-39 % spread) by absolute values; mark contribution 3 as open until the 128-user and x70 arms exist.

objections.title: TTFT of returning turns is not what the agent or the operator gets: turn latency and throughput do not move with hints
objections.claim_hit: Every TTFT comparison among the leading arms ('hints add 0.05-0.15 s', 'exact hints 0.20 s', 'ec_r13 first in both rows') and the choice of mean TTFT on shared returning turns as the headline metric (PAPER_PLAN contribution row 1, DECISIONS result tables).
objections.why_serious: Recomputed from client.jsonl. On the 11,198 turns the five leading arms share, mean turn latency (send to last token) is 12.05 s (JIT exact), 12.04 (ec_r13), 12.01 (nofc), 12.09 (nofc_noend), 12.31 (ec_r1). Paired ec_r13 - nofc_noend: TTFT -0.14 s but latency -0.05 s [-0.28,+0.18]; on the 6,715 turns TTFT -0.06 s but latency +0.20 s [-0.05,+0.47]. Exact hints against nofc_noend: TTFT -0.21 s, latency -0.05 [-0.28,+0.17] and -0.12 [-0.35,+0.06]. The TTFT gain is given back after the first token (+0.09 to +0.25 s); one run each cannot tell conservation of GPU work from noise (latency moved -0.01 to +0.61 s between reruns of the hint-free and JIT p50 arms). Throughput is equal: 11,700 / 11,690 / 11,716 / 11,680 turns sent before minute 115 (exact, ec_r13, nofc, nofc_noend), 2.37 M completion tokens each; the 11,000th turn went out at minute 108.7 / 108.7 / 108.4 / 108.8. The client is a closed loop at 44 sessions and the consumer is a tool harness, so latency, not the first token, sets progress. Mean TTFT is a tail statistic: medians are 0.266-0.278 s in all five arms, the two episodes (26.5 % of turns) hold 58-64 % of summed TTFT, the slowest 5 % of turns 49-53 %, and the median paired difference nofc_noend - ec_r13 is 6 ms. First turns are left out; on the 382 shared ones ec_r13 is 0.16 s slower than nofc_noend [-0.07,+0.44] and 0.21 s slower than nofc [+0.05,+0.46].
objections.how_to_answer: From client.jsonl on the same shared sets, per arm: mean, median, p90, p99 of latency and of latency - ttft; turns and completion_tokens with t_send < 6,900 s; share of turns with ttft over 2, 5 and 10 s (over 2 s: 5.6 % exact, 6.7 % ec_r13, 7.7 % nofc, 8.8 % nofc_noend; over 10 s: 118, 97, 197, 147 turns); the same with turn 0 included; paired differences by the block bootstrap with the same-arm pairs beside them. Lead with latency and throughput against original HiCache (25.8-29.9 s -> 11.5-11.8 s per turn; 6,956-7,541 -> 11,680 turns) and give TTFT as the diagnostic. My scripts and outputs: /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/verify/reviewer/review1.py and review3.py (.out beside them).

objections.title: One run per leading arm, an interval that fails on same-arm pairs, and a repeat rule that cannot decide with two runs
objections.claim_hit: DECISIONS 'ec_r13 is ahead of ec_r1, nofc and nofc_noend by 0.10, 0.11 and 0.14 s', 'not separated from exact hints', 'rule 3 adds 0.01 to 0.10 s', 'the end signal is worth 0.03 s', and the stated rule for reading ec_r13_rep and nofc_rep.
objections.why_serious: Each leading arm (ec_r13, ec_r1, nofc, nofc_noend) and JIT exact has one run. The within-pair block bootstrap is not a test: for the same arm run twice it excludes zero in base_rep - baseline (+1.15 s [+0.29,+2.25]), hintfree_ctl - hintfree on the 6,715 turns (+0.28 [+0.01,+0.65]) and jit_p50_d_cut - jit_p50_ctl in the first episode (+0.26 [+0.03,+0.48]). Reruns across dates moved 16-19 % of the arm's mean on the 6,715 turns (1.15 of 6.05 s, 0.28 of 1.75, 0.25 of 1.48); the one same-day same-unit pair moved 3 % but covers 75 minutes. At 0.7-0.9 s that is 0.02-0.17 s, against claimed differences of 0.05-0.14 s; I could not separate GPU unit from run-to-run variation with one same-unit pair. The differences rest on few events: the effective number of 500-position blocks is 8 of 22 for nofc_noend - ec_r13 and 5 for nofc - ec_r13 (top 3 blocks hold 52 % and 63 %); nofc and ec_r13 read from SSD on 1,581 and 1,582 turns but on different ones (544 only in nofc, 545 only in ec_r13). 1,218 of the 11,198 turns (10.9 %, minutes 100-115) have no position in the order run: they enter the bootstrap as one block and the tables as 'elsewhere' (0.40-0.46 s with them, 0.36-0.42 s without). The pre-written rule for repeats (all pairs one sign and smallest gap above the largest rerun move) with two runs per arm fires in 9 % of trials when there is no difference and in 16 %, 36 %, 59 % when the true gap is 1, 2, 3 run-to-run sd; with three runs per arm it fires in 0.8 % and in 12 % at 2 sd (Monte Carlo, normal noise). nofc_noend, against which the hint's value is measured, has no repeat queued, nor has JIT exact, and after the outage every remaining arm runs on GPU-a7198925 while the four leading arms ran on GPU-605dfc41.
objections.how_to_answer: Run the two arms that carry the hint-value claim until each has at least 4 runs (4 give 66 % power at a 2-sd gap in a t test on run means, 6 give 88 %), alternating A B A B on one GPU unit, fields '44 70 0 dist 0.1 10 <engine> 7200', arm three_tier_wc_oracle_v2_nu_owned: ec_r13 on engine_ec_20261111d with --hicache-storage-next-turn-read-timing expected_cost --hicache-storage-next-turn-memory-price 5e-5 --radix-eviction-policy return_chance --radix-eviction-policy-config {"horizon_s":30}; nofc_noend on engine_ec_20261111e with --hicache-storage-next-turn-read-timing arrival --radix-eviction-policy return_chance --radix-eviction-policy-config {"score":"queue"}. Test per-run means (whole run and the two episodes) with a permutation or t test; show the block bootstrap only beside the same-arm pairs; take positions from an order that covers every shared turn (JIT exact's send order).

objections.title: The scarce 'room' the design prices is a configuration artifact: a 70 GB host pool is the GPU's mirror plus 44K tokens
objections.claim_hit: Formulation sections 1, 5 and 7 (R = C_host - C_GPU = 43,968 tokens; '44 users, 70 GB: the host room binds'); PAPER_INTRO contribution 3 ('a forecast's errors are paid in shared host memory'); contribution 1 read as a property of three-tier caches.
objections.why_serious: From client.jsonl, sampled every 30 s: sessions in progress hold a median 1.15 M tokens of context (p90 1.27 M, peak 1.40 M = 138 GB of KV; shared prefixes counted per session) in every arm. The 70 GB pool holds 0.712 M; the 160 GB pool of the other setting holds 1.63 M, above the peak in every sample, so at 44 users in-progress history would need no SSD read. Without write-through's mirror the two pools hold 0.668 M + 0.712 M = 1.38 M distinct tokens, above the p90. PAPER_PLAN item 4 already says removing the mirror cuts SSD reads more than any hint and leaves it untested (lookup bug). The room limits every arm, hints or not: with exact hints 232 reading turns had a launch refused and 78 turns recomputed 8K tokens or more (72 % of that arm's recomputation). A reviewer will ask why the pool is not given 70 GB more (the host has 206 GB of RAM) or the mirror dropped, before 44K tokens are priced.
objections.how_to_answer: 44 users, x10, seed 0, host pool 160 GB and 100 GB (queue field host_gb), 2 h each: original HiCache (three_tier_wc on engine_5df71c4bf0_v2), nofc_noend and ec_r13 (12 h; 160 GB first). Report TTFT, latency, share of turns reading from SSD and refused launches against pool size. Chosen because pool size is the variable the formulation says sets the price, and no run varies it at fixed users. Then either show the band of pool sizes where the policy matters, or motivate a binding room by the workload (long contexts) instead of a small pool; add a write_back arm at 70 GB once ORACLE_FINDINGS issue 7 is fixed.

objections.title: Neither setting tests the stated problem: the SSD is mostly idle at 44 users, the GPU queue decides at 128, and x10 is where the paper's own numbers say recency already works
objections.claim_hit: PAPER_INTRO paragraphs 2-3, Figure 1 and contribution 1 (the slow tier on the critical path; 'idle time says little about return'); the motivation of rule 3; the reach of every 44-user result.
objections.why_serious: At 44 users and 70 GB the read thread is busy 16-21 % of the run in the four new arms (1,083-1,447 s of 6,900 s; device bytes read equal the engine's pages, ratio 1.00 against iostat, so the page cache is not a hidden tier), and DECISIONS puts all that read timing can win at 0.17 s per turn, of which rule 1 wins 0.045 s. At 128 users and 160 GB queue wait is 20.5-20.9 s of about 21 s. Figure 1 (SSD at 2.1 GB/s for an hour, then over 120 s) is campaign 14's old client with a backlog cap; on the current client x70 at 128 users showed no storm (campaign 18: 1.09 s, 0.58 s with exact hints; taken from the project notes, not recomputed by me). The trace study behind rule 3 gives LRU an AUC of 0.922 at x10 against 0.952 for the return-chance order, and 0.763 against 0.900 at x70: the evaluated gap scale is the one where a forecast should add least to eviction, and in the runs it adds nothing to the number of reading turns (1,582 against 1,581). At x10, 30 % of returning turns follow gaps under 2 s and 48 % gaps of 5-10 s (0.5-1 s in the trace's own time); turns after gaps of 30 s or more are 5.8 % of turns, 53 % of idle time and 27 % of reading turns.
objections.how_to_answer: x70 gaps, 128 users, 160 GB (campaign 18's setting; queue fields '128 - <oracle_hints> <hints> 0.1 70'), 2 h each: nofc_noend (engine_ec_20261111e, flags as at 44 users), ec_r13 or ec_r134, JIT exact ('1 oracle', no extra flag), original HiCache. Chosen because there reads are frequent, the room is 959K tokens and the GPU is not saturated, so read timing and eviction order are the levers; it is the setting of Figure 1 and of the AUC gap. If nofc_noend ties the hinted arms there as well, no measured setting supports the hint; if it does not, that setting is the paper's evidence and 44 users becomes the negative result.

objections.title: No rule is isolated: rule 1 mostly declines to act, rule 3 reads as often as LRU with ended sessions first, and the queued ec_r3 cannot separate them
objections.claim_hit: Formulation rules 1 and 3 (the read lands at the quantile q = lambda L / (1 + lambda L); evict by chance of return); DECISIONS 'JIT p50's loss is when its reads start, not its eviction order' and 'rule 3 adds 0.01 to 0.10 s'; PAPER_PLAN 'rule 3 at least as important as rule 1'.
objections.why_serious: From ec_r13's ec_start lines: 2,667 decisions, 629 staged reads. Of its 1,582 reading turns on the 11,198 shared turns, 212 (13 %) had every read landed by arrival; 775 (49 %) arrived while rule 1 was still waiting, 208 (13 %) had been left to arrival, 82 had no decision. The turns it staged carry 0.029 s of its 0.114 s lead over nofc and 0.023 s of 0.143 s over nofc_noend; 107-122 % of the lead is on turns that read nothing in ec_r13, so it comes from which histories were in memory, not from when reads start. Rule 1 against never staging: ec_r1 - nofc is -0.014 s TTFT [-0.10,+0.05] and +0.31 s latency [+0.13,+0.53]. Rule 3: 1,582 reading turns (ec_r13), 1,581 (nofc: LRU, ended first), 1,572 (ec_r1: next use from the p50); only the end signal moves the count (1,898 without). The replay ranked rule 3 at least as high as rule 1; ec_r1 at 0.67 s says the reverse. ec_r1 also differs from JIT p50 in at least four things besides the start rule (a plan lives 1,800 s instead of ending the session at p50 + max(60 s, p50); pins released once the entry has passed; at most two stagings; a queue-wait estimate that counts only GPU-bound queues). The queued ec_r3 puts rule 3 under JIT p50's p10 timing, already 0.64-0.89 s behind, so it cannot show what rule 3 adds to a sound read rule.
objections.how_to_answer: Complete the 2x2 of read start by eviction score on engine_ec_20261111d, arm three_tier_wc_oracle_v2_nu_owned, fields '44 70 0 dist 0.1 10 engine_ec_20261111d 7200': (a) rule 3 with reads at arrival: --hicache-storage-next-turn-read-timing arrival --radix-eviction-policy return_chance --radix-eviction-policy-config {"horizon_s":30}; (b) rule 1 with the forecast-free order: --hicache-storage-next-turn-read-timing expected_cost --hicache-storage-next-turn-memory-price 5e-5 --radix-eviction-policy return_chance --radix-eviction-policy-config {"score":"lru"}. Both pass the validation hooks in hicache_hook.py and kv_cache_hook.py as I read them (confirm with checks/validate_queue.py). If only one arm fits, run (a) in place of ec_r3.

objections.title: The exact-hint reference is one run from 2026-11-01 on another GPU unit and build, and the policy's exact-hint limit has never been run
objections.claim_hit: The 'share of the gain' column (100 % = JIT exact); DECISIONS 'ec_r13 keeps pace with exact hints / not separated from exact hints' and 'exact hints are 0.06 s ahead of ec_r13 and 0.18 s ahead of nofc: the whole prize a gap forecast can still win'; Formulation section 6 ('with exact hints rule 1 is JIT exact and rule 3 is Belady').
objections.why_serious: JIT exact ran on GPU-b59d6a34 with engine_owned_20261101; the ec arms ran ten days later on GPU-605dfc41 with engine d. Same-arm pairs across those dates moved 8-19 % of their mean. ec_r13 - exact is +0.149 s [+0.08,+0.23] on the 6,715 turns (0.66 against 0.51 s, 29 % slower; first episode 1.56 against 1.14 s) but +0.063 s [-0.01,+0.14] on the 11,198, because in the second episode ec_r13 is ahead of exact hints (1.80 against 1.93 s; blocks -0.58 and -0.16 s). A three-quantile forecast beating the exact one means either the episode-level differences are run noise or 'exact' is not an upper bound; either way 'reaches exact' and 'the whole prize is 0.06 s' are not established. No arm runs expected_cost or return_chance on exact hints, so the stated limit is derivation only.
objections.how_to_answer: Two arms on the current unit, arm three_tier_wc_oracle_v2_nu_owned, fields '44 70 1 oracle 0.1 10 engine_ec_20261111d 7200': (a) jit_exact_d with no extra flag, which re-anchors the 100 % mark on this build and unit; (b) ec_r13_exact with --hicache-storage-next-turn-read-timing expected_cost --hicache-storage-next-turn-memory-price 5e-5 --radix-eviction-policy return_chance --radix-eviction-policy-config {"horizon_s":30}, which should equal (a) within the rerun spread if the limit holds (the engine builds a point distribution for exact hints).

objections.title: The price was fitted on the evaluated turns, has no sensitivity run, and the learning rule as stated collapses on the run's own signals
objections.claim_hit: Rule 1's lambda = 5e-5 and section 7 ('a 64K-token read should land near p75-p80'); rule 4 (dual ascent on the room; 'one code path serves both settings'); section 5's Whittle relaxation; the claim of four rules (rules 2 and 4 have no run, per-key recalibration is not built).
objections.why_serious: lambda came from the CPU room model replaying jit_p50_c44 and jit_exact_c44, the same seed-0 turns the arms are scored on; the 30 s horizon and the queue-wait fix came from the same logs. In that model the best lambda moves from 1e-4 to 2e-5 between rooms of 70K and 110K tokens, and the measured idle room is 54K at the median and 75K on average. Replayed on ec_r13's ec_price signals, rule 4 as stated falls to its floor (1e-7) in 0.6 min and stays there in 77 % of intervals (7.7K tokens refused against 74.7K idle per interval; excess above zero in 9 %); the 'harm' rule that replaces it was written after reading that log and has no closed-loop run yet. With R = 44K and reads of 17-19K tokens the room holds two or three histories, so the many-small-sessions premise of the relaxation does not apply, and the cost model takes the queue as given although DECISIONS finds a recomputed token costs 6-8 times its own prefill through the queue. Since never staging ties rule 1 (0.014 s), the price may not be identified at all at this setting. Nothing could be checked for rules 2 and 4: no run exists.
objections.how_to_answer: Two price arms beside ec_r13 (engine_ec_20261111d, same other flags): --hicache-storage-next-turn-memory-price 5e-6 and --hicache-storage-next-turn-memory-price 5e-4. Report TTFT, latency, staged reads and refused launches. When ec_r134 lands, plot its ec_price trajectory against refusals and say whether it leaves 5e-5. If TTFT is flat over 100x of price, state that the price is not identified at 44 users and move the pricing claim to a setting where staging pays; score the final constants on a seed the model never saw.

objections.title: One trace, one seed, gaps stretched tenfold; the forecast is sharp where no read is needed and loose where one is; reply key and end signal come from the replay
objections.claim_hit: 'Realistic' three-quantile hints (PAPER_PLAN contribution rows 'what a realistic forecast costs' and 'the conditional table'); PAPER_PLAN needed item 3 (human-paced workload); the reach of every result.
objections.why_serious: Every arm replays seed 0 of one trace at x10 with the same sessions in the same order, so all evidence is two load episodes of one sequence (58-64 % of the leading arms' summed TTFT). From the dist_hint each turn carried (nofc_noend): before turns that read nothing the true gap is within 2 s of the p50 in 78 % and above the p90 in 10 %; before the 1,914 turns that read from SSD, 43 % and 27 % (below the p10: 2 %), with a p90 - p10 width of 12 s against 5.4 s (26 s in ec_r13). The table is learned online from the population it predicts; the engine takes the reply key from the client (hicache_storage_next_turn_reply_key_source = hint in server_args), so it never parses its own reply; every recorded end is signalled. No run uses a human-paced or long-context trace (PAPER_PLAN cites 92 % human waiting and 126K-token contexts; here a reading turn loads 17-19K tokens).
objections.how_to_answer: Same 44 users, 70 GB, x10 with SEED=1 and SEED=2 (needs a launcher variant: c26.sh fixes SEED=0): original HiCache, nofc_noend, ec_r13, 2 h each, to show the episodes and the order of arms are not properties of one sequence. Then one arm with the reply key parsed by the engine (reply key source 'reply') and one with the hint table frozen from another seed. Seeds first because they cost no engineering; the human-paced trace of item 3 remains needed. From existing logs, publish the calibration split above for every hinted arm.

objections.title: The one setting where hints looked decisive, 128 users, still has no fair rival, no repeat and only cross-unit references
objections.claim_hit: PAPER_PLAN 'at 128 users the hint-free arm keeps about 58 % of the gain and p50 hints keep nearly all the rest (12.14, 12.56 s)' and 'worth up to 16.6-17.1 s per turn'; PAPER_INTRO 'realistic forecasts keep nearly all of the 128-user gain'.
objections.why_serious: The 29.19 s hint-free arm lacks the queue-state mechanisms; at 44 users those are worth 1.02 s (1.95 -> 0.93 s on 9,703 turns), more than everything hints add there. The three queued 128-user arms come last (about 11:00-17:10Z on 2026-11-12), have no same-unit run of a known hinted arm (ec_r134's price rule is itself untested), and 128 users has no rerun of any arm; the references (53.12 s, 12.06-12.56 s) are first-2-h slices of 5 h runs from 2026-10-18 to 11-04 on other units, among which a 0.4 s gap between routines is already unexplained. The difference of interest may be seconds there, which helps, but one run each will again be read against an unknown spread.
objections.how_to_answer: 128 users, 160 GB, x10 on one unit, 2 h each: nofc_noend_c128 twice (the same-arm pair), JIT p50 on engine_ec_20261111d with no extra flag (fields '128 - 0 dist 0.1 10'), and ec_r13 at the fixed 5e-5 beside ec_r134_c128. Report TTFT, queue wait, recomputed tokens, SSD pages and read-thread busy share on the turns all share. Until then write the 128-user hint value as 'at most 17 s per turn against an engine without queue-state protection; unmeasured against one with it'.

objections.title: The 'no hints' rival still uses the hint channel, bundles four mechanisms, and stands in for prior systems that are not compared
objections.claim_hit: DECISIONS 'with no hint at all the engine gets 96 %' and 'the difference between the two hint-free arms is the queue-state mechanisms, about 1.0 s'; PAPER_INTRO's positioning against CachedAttention, Bidaw, Continuum and Tokencake.
objections.why_serious: nofc_noend runs with HINTS=dist: its plan (session id, next request id, committed key) is created from the hint when the previous turn commits, and the arrival gate works only on a planned turn (prefetch_gate: without a plan 'only a lookup can tell'). It is a session-id-only client, not an unchanged one: one reviewer will say the rival is flattered, another that it is not hint-free. It differs from the earlier hint-free arm in engine build, pin fraction 0.3, deadline read order, gate, hold, queued-turn protection and re-reads together: 1.02 s with no step separated. PAPER_INTRO lists exactly these protections as 'no longer new' and says rule 3 'has to be compared with' Bidaw's hit potential, 'not only with LRU and point forecasts'; none of CachedAttention's look-ahead, Bidaw's eviction and read order, Continuum's TTL or Tokencake's point-timed upload is built.
objections.how_to_answer: Name the rival 'session id only' and present it as the CachedAttention-style baseline; take read pins and queued-turn protection out of the contributions; say which of gate, hold, protection and re-reads is untested alone. From existing logs, for hintfree_ctl against nofc_noend on their 9,703 shared turns give turns that shrank while queued (288 against 9), refused launches (238 against 293), recomputed tokens on reading turns (2,436 against 585) and ntp_gate decisions, to show through which mechanism the 1.0 s goes.

objections.title: The policy has recompute bursts of its own and queued-turn protection is soft; a mean over the returning turns of one run hides both
objections.claim_hit: Rule 2's 'do no harm'; DECISIONS 'a registration now covers the session's whole path' and 'fewer reads, almost no pins' for ec_r13; contribution 1's framing that the storm belongs to the baseline.
objections.why_serious: The one block where ec_r13 trails all three same-day arms (positions 3,000-3,500, minutes 30.0-31.2: 0.66 s against 0.42-0.44 s) recomputed 183K tokens against 15-18K in the others; 16 turns had launches refused. In server.log, c98-t43 arrived 7.7 s after its plan with 19.5K of 54K tokens already on SSD only, had three launches refused with 2.9K tokens pinned, lost its GPU prefix while queued (matched 34,496 -> 11,648) and recomputed 42.5K tokens: TTFT 15.7 s against 0.35 s under ec_r1. Turns that shrank while queued: 17 (ec_r13), 15 (ec_r1), 18 (exact), 7 and 9 (the rivals). In every leading arm 70-105 turns with 8K or more recomputed tokens hold 72-77 % of recomputation and 7-10 % of summed TTFT, and 65-98 of them had a launch refused; the slowest 1 % of turns carry 21-24 % of each arm's TTFT. I did not establish why that prefix was evicted (rule 3's order, or nothing else left to evict).
objections.how_to_answer: Per run: (1) from client.jsonl, turns with max(reply_reprefilled, 0) >= 8,000: count, tokens, summed ttft; (2) from server.log, the conv-turn ids with any 'HICACHE_EVT srs_dispatch ... launched=0', joined to (1); (3) 60-s windows by t_send with over 50K recomputed tokens, listed by position, and whether the other arms have one at the same positions; (4) for each such window the evict_device and evict_host tokens inside it, and for its worst turn the ReqTimeStats queue_duration and forward_duration. Report p99, maximum and turns over 10 s beside every mean (ec_r13 97, exact 118, nofc_noend 147, nofc 197 on the 11,198 turns).

supported_claims: Original HiCache collapses at 44 users / 70 GB and every arm with read pins does not: 5.47 and 6.62 s against 1.89 s or less on the 6,715 shared returning turns; all run pairs have one sign and the smallest gap (3.59 s) is 3x the baseline's own rerun move (1.15 s). It holds on other metrics too: 25.8-29.9 s against 11.5-15.9 s mean turn latency, 6,956-7,541 against 10,037-11,716 turns sent before minute 115.
PAPER_PLAN's 79 %: read pins without hints give 72-82 % of the way from original HiCache to exact hints (hint-free 1.61 and 1.89 s; two runs on each side).

A p50 forecast acted on as exact is no better than pins alone (JIT p50 1.35 and 1.60 s against hint-free 1.61 and 1.89 s) and is worse than every arm that stages little or nothing: nofc_noend, ec_r13 and JIT exact are 0.64-1.02 s ahead of each of three JIT p50 runs, 3-5x the JIT p50 rerun move (0.18 s). Its mechanisms repeat (staged reads 2,094 and 2,202; launches refused 1,743 and 1,732; mean pins 30.2K and 31.5K tokens), and the new build is not the cause (jit_p50_d_cut - jit_p50_ctl = +0.05 s [-0.04,+0.15] over the first 75 minutes; the second episode is not covered).

PAPER_PLAN's caution that hint-free shares are floors because that arm lacks queue-state mechanisms: at 44 users those mechanisms are worth 1.02 s (1.95 -> 0.93 s on 9,703 turns; turns that shrank while queued 288 -> 9), one run each, not separated from one another.

The replay's negative predictions held on the GPU: rule 1 ties reading at arrival once recomputation is charged for the queue (ec_r1 0.67 against nofc 0.69 s; 0.86 against 0.88 s); read timing alone does not reach exact hints; most of rule 3's gain is the end signal (reading turns 1,898 without it, 1,581 with it, 1,582 with the three-quantile score).

Exact hints under the just-in-time routine are the best arm on TTFT: 0.20 s ahead of the no-hint rival on both turn sets (0.51 against 0.71 s; 0.70 against 0.91 s), same sign in 16 of 16 and 21 of 22 blocks. One run from another date and unit, and not visible in turn latency (-0.05 to -0.12 s, intervals cover zero).

Hints reduce SSD read traffic at 44 users, one run each: 562K pages with no hint, 469K with the end signal (-17 %), 437K with three quantiles (-22 %), 388K with exact hints (-31 %). The read thread is 16-21 % busy there, so nothing follows for latency.

The measurement plumbing is sound: I reproduced the 6,715 / 11,198 / 9,702 / 6,579 shared sets and every arm's mean on them; decode step, first-turn prefill and SSD ms per page agree within 1-3 % across arms in matched windows; bytes read from the device equal the engine's s2h pages x 6.29 MB (ratio 1.00), so the page cache is not a hidden tier; no client errors in any of the 12 runs.
DECISIONS' own reading rule 'a difference under about 0.25 s is not a result on one run each' is consistent with the same-arm pairs (0.25, 0.28 and 1.15 s on the 6,715 turns).
contradicted_claims: Contradicted: PAPER_PLAN 'The claim' and contribution row 1, that forecasts from the agent drive the gain. At 44 users / 70 GB an engine with no gap forecast and no end signal is at 0.71 s against 5.47-6.62 s for original HiCache and 0.51 s for exact hints (96 %); three-quantile hints add 0.05 s (6,715 turns) to 0.14 s (11,198 turns), about one rerun move.

Contradicted: PAPER_INTRO 'once landed reads are protected, exact return times cut mean TTFT a further 2.9x [1.47 -> 0.50 s]' and PAPER_PLAN 'exact hints add 0.96 s'. Against a hint-free engine that also protects queued turns, exact hints are worth 0.20 s (0.71 -> 0.51 s, 1.4x).

Contradicted: PAPER_PLAN contribution row 'where the gain comes from' (just-in-time timing 18 %, gate and hold 4 %). With nofc_noend as the hint-free step, exact-hint timing is 0.20 s of about 5-6 s (3-4 %).

The first half holds (it is worse than none, by 0.64-0.89 s). The recovery is matched with no distribution and no price (nofc 0.69, nofc_noend 0.71 against ec_r13 0.66 s).

Unsupported: rule 2 (soft pins) and per-key recalibration (no run, the latter not built); the Whittle argument (the room holds two or three histories); the cost model's 'queue taken as given' (queue wait is where arms differ: JIT p50 is 0.25 s of queue and 0.27 s after admission behind exact hints).

Unsupported: PAPER_PLAN contribution rows 'latency against load' (knee shifts of 3-5 %, 6 %, 11 % read from swings in single runs; no user-count sweep) and 'the conditional table' (the engine has never read its own reply on a GPU; these runs take the reply key from the client).

Unsupported: PAPER_INTRO paragraph 2-3 as the setting of the evaluation. Figure 1 is campaign 14's old client; in the current-code settings the read thread is 16-21 % busy (44 users) or the GPU queue decides (128 users); 'idle time says little about return' holds at x70 (LRU AUC 0.763), not at the evaluated x10 (0.922).
defensible_headline: On one H200 with 44 concurrent agent sessions, a 70 GB host pool and tool gaps stretched x10 (one trace, one seed, 2 h runs), SGLang's three-tier HiCache spends its load episodes recomputing history it had already read back: mean TTFT of returning turns 5.5 and 6.6 s in two runs, 25.8-29.9 s per turn end to end, 7,541 and 6,956 turns served. Protecting what queued turns need (read pins, queued-turn eviction protection, an arrival gate and hold, re-reads; no gap forecast and no end signal) brings this to 0.71 s (7.7-9.3x lower), 11.6 s per turn and 11,680 turns (+55 to +68 %), 96 % of the way to exact next-arrival hints (0.51 s). Acting on a p50 forecast as if it were exact is worse than not forecasting (1.35-1.60 s in three runs, the new build included). Three-quantile forecasts under rules 1 and 3 add 0.05-0.15 s of TTFT and 22 % fewer SSD pages over that rival in one run each: a margin not yet separated from the 0.25-0.28 s that reruns of one arm moved, and not visible in turn latency or throughput.
missing_from_plan: A host-memory sweep at fixed users and a non-mirroring write policy: in-progress context peaks at 1.40 M tokens (138 GB) against a 0.712 M pool; a 160 GB pool holds 1.63 M, and GPU plus host without the mirror 1.38 M. Neither the plan nor the queue varies pool size at 44 users.

End-to-end metrics as primary results: turn latency, turns and tokens per hour, share of turns within a TTFT target, p99 and maximum, first turns included; and one open-loop arrival run, since the closed loop at 44 sessions slows its own offered load when an arm is slow.
A repeat of nofc_noend (the queue repeats nofc only) and a rerun of JIT exact on the current build and unit; a same-arm pair at 128 users; enough runs per arm for a test on run means (4-6).
The planned user-count sweep compares the best routine with original HiCache; it needs nofc_noend as the comparison, or it will measure the protection mechanisms again and not the hint.

The 2x2 of read start by eviction score (reads at arrival with the return-chance score; rule 1 with the forecast-free order), exact hints under the new rules, and sensitivity to the price and the 30 s horizon on turns the tuning never saw.

Each queue-state mechanism alone (queued-turn protection, gate, hold, re-reads), and head-to-head runs against CachedAttention-style look-ahead and Bidaw's hit-potential eviction and read order built in the same engine.

Other seeds and traces, a long-context or human-paced workload, a second model or GPU, and a faster SSD: at 2.3-2.5 GB/s the read itself is 0.7 s of a 2.0-2.4 s stall, so a local NVMe shrinks the only quantity read timing can remove.

Forecast robustness and incentives: a stale or shifted table, wrong keys, missing end signals, the engine parsing its own reply, and a client that reports short gaps to keep its history in host memory at other tenants' cost.
Policy overhead: per-tick cost of rules 1 and 3 with 128 or more plans, and hint bytes per request (3 KB today).

SSD write volume and the full-volume regime: write-through wrote about 1.2 TB per 115 min at 44 users (about 15 TB per day on a 2.3 TB volume); starting from an empty volume a 2 h arm stays near half full, below the cleaner's 70 % mark, so the cleaner never runs in these arms.
Steady state: every arm is a 2 h cold start with two transient episodes; no run is long enough to average over many episodes or to show recovery after one.
More than one GPU or replica: the prefetcher refuses multi-rank setups, and there is no account of a router in front of several engines.

Reproducibility: the engine is uncommitted and frozen/ is outside git; four engine freezes on the day of the runs with reviewer-found logic defects and two known ones left; PAPER_PLAN still quotes numbers from deleted runs (the p50's 87 %, the oracle's 0.05-0.14 s spread); GPU units are unrecorded for campaigns 19-21.

Limits of this review (not a plan item): I ran only CPU scripts on the 12 finished runs (/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/verify/reviewer/, review1-8.py with .out files); I did not read the run in progress, could not check rules 2 and 4 (no runs), could not separate GPU-unit from run-to-run effects, and took campaign 18's x70 figures and the AUC values from the project's notes and PAPER_PLAN without recomputing them.
